requirements.requirement: The repaired consumer must remain running across producer disconnects so successive producers can submit jobs without restarting it.
requirements.summary: The original consumer was directly shown to exit after the first producer, leaving the next producer blocked. After repair, live tests before and after reboot showed one consumer surviving multiple successive producers and accepting records from each.

requirements.requirement: Append each complete newline-delimited job ID to received.txt, ignore empty and incomplete lines, and preserve existing records.
requirements.summary: Tests submitted valid lines, blank lines, and unterminated fragments. Exact comparisons showed only the valid complete lines appended. Prefix hashes proved preservation of the original 13-byte record and all subsequently accumulated records.

requirements.requirement: Avoid a busy loop while no producer is connected.
requirements.summary: Repeated observations found the idle consumer sleeping in wait_for_partner with zero CPU-tick growth over bounded idle intervals.
Three live tests directly observed SIGTERM exit status 0 and no remaining consumer process.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 before and after execution. The repaired script compiled and ran successfully using the installed Python 3.12.9; package health also remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The repaired consumer handles successive producer connections, records only complete non-empty lines while preserving prior data, blocks efficiently when idle, and terminates cleanly. The platform was retained, and the required node restart protocol demonstrated persistence and recovery.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the application files themselves; post-restart application persistence is established by direct executor checksum and behavioral observations instead.
The initial discovery output was truncated, but the decisive baseline failure, repaired behavior, restart transition, and final state are present in separate complete evidence records.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had a supported role: the isolated sandbox reproduced the defect and was removed; consumer.py was safely replaced with metadata and label preservation; a root-only rollback copy was retained as editing protection; test records were bounded functional evidence; generated caches and temporary test files were removed; and the reboot implemented the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutation was identified. Final observations showed no test residue, failed services, new listeners, package damage, weakened SELinux state, or stray consumer process. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, persisted code/data, recovered SSH, and successful post-reboot application behavior.
